The new sheet: Sonnet 5.5 and the algorithm

Implementation 03, Phase 4. Sonnet 5.5 reads each song window by window (12 to 16 seconds) and decides the hands, the beam groups, the clefs and 8va, the ornaments and the armadura of each passage; it also chose the reference figure of each song. The app then computes the figures, the grace notes and the accidentals by its rules, cuts a beam group where the figures break it (one figure per group), and joins nearby 8va notes into one line. Each case shows the same passage written by the algorithm (the sheet the app shows at once) and by Sonnet (what replaces it, segment by segment). The band marks the passage. Please judge the beam groups (the criteria of the plan, section 3.11, and the maximum of 8 notes), the hands and the clefs.

Beam groups

1. A repeated bass pattern: one group per repetition

Left hand: an octave bass pattern that repeats. Sonnet makes one group of four notes for each repetition, so the eye sees the same shape again and again; the algorithm runs groups of seven and eight notes across the repetitions. The right hand's repeated notes are in groups of four too.

Poker Face — Lady Gaga, from 0:32 (columns f800 to f1049). Reference figure: negra 500 ms, corchea 250 ms, semicorchea 125 ms. Differences in the passage: 0 notes in another hand, 24 beam joins, 0 clef changes.

2. An arpeggio that rises and falls

Left hand: a broken chord that goes up and comes down. Sonnet makes one group for each rise and fall and cuts where the next chord starts; the algorithm cuts at other places. The clef changes inside the arpeggio are rule clef.L4 (see the section on clefs).

Halleluyah - Pinchivi, from 1:12 (columns f1800 to f2049). Reference figure: negra 700 ms, corchea 350 ms, semicorchea 175 ms. Differences in the passage: 8 notes in another hand, 25 beam joins, 5 clef changes.

3. Short-long pairs in the melody

Right hand: a semicorchea beamed to the corchea after it, the rhythm of the melody. A pair of two figures is allowed by your rule (one note of another figure may open a group). The left hand's small notes before its chords are acciaccaturas by the rule (octaves played unevenly).

7 Years — Lukas Graham, from 2:52 (columns f4300 to f4549). Reference figure: negra 480 ms, corchea 240 ms, semicorchea 120 ms. Differences in the passage: 5 notes in another hand, 19 beam joins, 0 clef changes.

4. Chords in groups, and the left hand kept in its clef

Right hand: repeated chords grouped by four, then a new group where the chord changes. Left hand: the algorithm moves some chords to the right hand (a bass clef in the upper staff) and jumps to the treble clef; Sonnet keeps the bass and chord pattern in the left hand, in the bass clef.

Birds of a Feather, from 2:36 (columns f3900 to f4149). Reference figure: negra 580 ms, corchea 290 ms, semicorchea 145 ms. Differences in the passage: 12 notes in another hand, 11 beam joins, 4 clef changes.

Hands

5. Low chords of the accompaniment go to the left hand

The algorithm gives low chords to the right hand, below the treble staff with ledger lines. Sonnet gives them to the left hand (a bass note and a chord, beamed in pairs), and the right hand keeps the melody. 224 notes of this song changed hand, the most of the 10 songs.

Hips Don't Lie — Shakira, from 1:00 (columns f1500 to f1749). Reference figure: negra 600 ms, corchea 300 ms, semicorchea 150 ms. Differences in the passage: 23 notes in another hand, 41 beam joins, 0 clef changes.

6. A clean split between melody and accompaniment

The algorithm puts very low notes in the right hand (five ledger lines below the staff) and makes the left hand jump between clefs. Sonnet keeps the melody and its chords in the right hand and the accompaniment in the left hand, in the bass clef. The wavy line before a wide chord is a rolled chord (arp), which Sonnet wrote 85 times in this song.

Moonlight Shadow — Mike Oldfield, from 0:46 (columns f1150 to f1399). Reference figure: negra 480 ms, corchea 240 ms, semicorchea 120 ms. Differences in the passage: 26 notes in another hand, 15 beam joins, 10 clef changes.

7. A right hand that stays in the treble clef

In the second line the algorithm gives a low note to the right hand and needs a bass clef in the upper staff for it; Sonnet gives that note to the left hand, and both staves keep their clef.

Drivers License — Olivia Rodrigo, from 2:36 (columns f3900 to f4149). Reference figure: negra 420 ms, corchea 210 ms, semicorchea 105 ms. Differences in the passage: 10 notes in another hand, 1 beam joins, 2 clef changes.

8. Chords that belong to the left hand

The algorithm moves the chords of the accompaniment to the right hand and changes the upper staff to the bass clef twice; Sonnet keeps them in the left hand under a right hand that stays in the treble clef.

The One That Got Away — Katy Perry, from 1:26 (columns f2150 to f2399). Reference figure: negra 420 ms, corchea 210 ms, semicorchea 105 ms. Differences in the passage: 14 notes in another hand, 1 beam joins, 2 clef changes.

Clefs and 8va (a question for you)

9. A high cover: long 8va lines, and a left hand that changes clef often

This cover is played high. The right hand is under 8va lines (Sonnet marked the high notes; the app joins nearby 8va notes into one line). The left hand alternates low notes and high chords about twice a second, and your rule clef.L4 puts the low notes in the bass clef and the chords in the treble clef, so the clef changes very often. Do you want this, or the chords in the bass clef with ledger lines?

AITANA - SUPERESTRELLA | PIANO TUTORIAL / COVER, from 0:58 (columns f1450 to f1699). Reference figure: negra 440 ms, corchea 220 ms, semicorchea 110 ms. Differences in the passage: 18 notes in another hand, 5 beam joins, 4 clef changes.

Figures of staccato notes (a question for you)

10. Short notes become fusas and semifusas

The left hand plays short detached notes a corchea apart. Their figure comes from their own length (your rule), so they are fusas and semifusas with three or four beams, which reads as a very fast passage. Sonnet cannot change figures: they are a rule of the app.
